text:
**For a full recharge in one day, plan on roughly 300-350 W of solar panels. If you can wait a day or two, 200 W works.**

**The formula** (from [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):
panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.75)

The 0.75 covers real-world losses from heat, panel angle, and charge-controller conversion. Other sources use 0.7 to 0.75.

**Panel watts to refill 1,000 Wh from empty in one day:**

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter, cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230 W |

Source: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) gets a similar ~300 W for a summer day. It says the same job takes 700 W or more in a northern winter.

**If you're fine with 1-2 days:**
- A 200 W panel yields about 630 Wh per day at 4.5 peak sun hours and 70% efficiency. That refills 1,000 Wh in about 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A quick rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, which gives about 200 W.
- A 400 W panel setup does it in about 1.5 days even at the 2,000 Wh scale, so on 1,000 Wh it takes under a day ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Things to check before buying:**
- **Station solar input limit:** Panels above this limit add nothing. Mid-range 1,000-1,500 Wh stations often accept 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage window:** Panels wired in series add voltage. Keep the combined open-circuit voltage (Voc) within your station's accepted range, or you risk damaging the charge controller ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)). Parallel wiring is generally safer for beginners.
- **Running loads while charging:** Net charge is solar input minus whatever you're drawing, so recharging will be slower.
- **Aim the panels:** Re-angling them toward the sun a few times a day can add 20-30%.

**One option if you need a panel:** the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is listed at $299 (about $269 with code ALLPOWERS26, per [Dealectric's code listing](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-discount-codes)). That's an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy. It only makes sense if your station accepts 400 W of input, and it may not be compatible with other brands. Check your station's spec sheet first.
